name: LlamaDB
tagline: Hobby SQL database in Rust built to learn SQL internals; archived and explicitly not for real use.
description: LlamaDB is a learning project by Dan Spencer, started in 2015 when Rust was barely 1.0, to understand how SQL databases work and to test whether Rust suited large systems software. It implements a SQL parser, a query planner and executor, and a B-tree storage layer modelled on SQLite's documentation, with a small CLI prompt for running queries. The author states plainly that it will never be production-ready. Development ended in 2017 and the repository is archived, but it remains a readable, MIT-licensed example of a from-scratch SQL engine in early Rust.
statusNote: Hobby project, archived on GitHub; last commit Dec 2017. The author marks it unmaintained and not for real use.
strengths: Compact, readable SQL parser, planner and executor in Rust
B-tree design modelled on SQLite's documented format
Permissive MIT license for reuse in teaching
weaknesses: Written against pre-stable nightly Rust; needs work to build today
useCases: Studying how a small SQL engine is put together
Historical example of early systems programming in Rust
